name: lib/chaos-engine
title: Chaos engine
summary: A seeded, deterministic fault schedule (errors, latency, timeouts, unreachable) for chaos tests. It decides which fault the next call gets; the host injects it. It refuses to run in production.

config.name: seed
config.description: Same seed, same faults, in every build.

config.name: unreachable_rate
config.description: Probability of refusing the connection. Each rate is in [0, 1] and the four sum to at most 1.

config.name: error_rate
config.description: Probability of failing with a 5xx from error_statuses.

config.name: latency_rate
config.description: Probability of a delay in [latency_min_ms, latency_max_ms].

operations.description: Refuses production (and any unknown environment) and an invalid plan.
None, Latency{ms}, Error{status}, Timeout or Unreachable. One unit draw picks the kind; an error or latency draws one more.

invariants.text: The same plan gives the same faults; a different seed gives different ones.
The sequence for each seed matches the vectors produced by an independent Python implementation, so every build reproduces it.
The generator is SplitMix64 and matches its published reference outputs.
Production, and any environment not plainly a test one (including empty), is refused. There is no override.
Rates outside [0, 1] or summing past 1, a backwards latency range and a bad status list are refused at construction.
A plan with no rates never injects anything.
A rate of 1 always injects that fault.
Injected latency stays inside its range and the observed rates match the plan.

gaps: No TypeScript or Python build yet (mzizi-registry#472, phases 1 and 2); __tests__/fixtures/chaos/seeded.json is what they will be held to.
The CLI command that runs a plan against a service (`mzizi chaos run`) is tracked in mzizi-dev/agent-tools#285.
Not a registry entry yet; mzizi-assurance's `mzizi-chaos` (blast-radius diagnostics) is a different thing and is not replaced.
